name: Ryan Peterson
strengths: Peterson chases with a high LB motor — works downhill, then still finishes pursuit to the perimeter on bounce runs.
Peterson fills assigned gaps with leverage and physicality, especially effective in short-yardage / early-down run fits.
Peterson wraps and finishes tackles instead of arm-grabbing — shows competitive contact through the ball carrier.
weaknesses: Peterson still needs cleaner hand counters when OL latch on reach/zone — can get washed before he sheds.
Peterson’s zone-drop footwork and depth timing need polish so windows underneath close faster in coverage.
comparison: Peterson comps to Ernest Jones — listed 6-0 / 220 vs Jones’ ~6-2 / 230 LB mold (height within ~2", same compact MIKE frame); then matching downhill fill, wrap tackle, and gap-sound traits (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Peterson projects to develop into Florida’s LB room with Year-1 special-teams / early-down run snaps, Year-2 compete for a rotational every-down MIKE/WILL role, and Year-3+ starter upside if the shed hands and coverage drops catch the motor.
schemeFit: Peterson fits an attacking 4-3 / nickel that wants a gap-sound MIKE who can fill downhill, wrap up, and still chase when the ball bounces.
staffNotes: FILM VERIFIED 2026-08-09 from William A. Hough sophomore highlights (Ryan Peterson #5, Sophomore Full SZN). Watched gameplay — downhill fill, pursuit, wrap; shed + coverage polish.
recruitingStory: Ryan Peterson is a 4-star LB listed 6-0 / 220 from William Amos Hough (Cornelius, NC) — national LB with Florida in the live chase mix.
angle: Compact MIKE with fill + finish traits Florida can develop into starter-upside linebacker play.
insiderNotes: Watched Hough sophomore tape. Peterson wins with fill and finish; next step is shedding and coverage depth.
